rights.note: The book is in copyright. These lessons teach the ideas of calculus in original wording with original scenarios and diagrams. They quote nothing from the book, do not follow its chapter order and reuse none of its stories, examples or figures; they name the book, the author and one term he coined. Not reviewed by a lawyer.

ideas.name: Cut, solve, add back
ideas.can: Spot when a problem can be cut into simple pieces, and say what the pieces are.

ideas.name: Slope at a point
ideas.can: Read the steepness of a curve at a point, and say what it means.

ideas.name: The derivative
ideas.can: Tell an average rate from an instantaneous one, and read each from a graph.

ideas.name: The integral
ideas.can: Estimate a total from a rate graph, and say whether an estimate runs high or low.

ideas.name: Rates and totals undo each other
ideas.can: Move between a rate and its running total, in either direction.

ideas.name: Laws written as rates
ideas.can: Recognise a rule-of-change description, and predict its short-term behaviour.
